title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-04-07
content:
Daily scratchpad - 2026-04-07
Owner: Jordan Reyes (eng-serving-runtime)

Quick summary:
- Short triage of a few regressions surfaced by nightly canary. Focus: perf regressions and a flaky fused-kernel path on A100s.
- Experiment plan for batching knob auto-tuner.
- Kernel and KV-cache notes to follow up with Luca.

Bugs / triage (high -> low):
1) JIRA-ENG-4321: increased tail latency on long-seq workloads since 2026-04-03 rollout
   - Observed: p95 up ~150ms on 4k sequences, p99 up ~400ms.
   - Suspect: fallback to scalar attention for specific sequence length boundary due to shape mismatch in fused kernel.
   - Repro: nightly-canary long-seq bench (link in linked_artifacts).
   - Next action: capture kernel selection logs for 4k cases, add extra instrumentation to measure time spent in fallback. Assign to Luca.

2) SDK retry storm on transient gRPC disconnects - small spike in requests that retried caused bursty batching leading to CPU thrash
   - Mitigation: short-term: add jitter to retry backoff in SDK (patch ready, PR 987).
   - Longer-term: rate-limit per-client burst in router.

Perf TODOs / experiments:
- Batching auto-tuner experiment:
  * Hypothesis: current static batch_size=64 is suboptimal for mixed short/long requests; auto-tuner using EWMA of queue depth should improve throughput without harming p50.
  * Plan: 2-week A/B test on 10% traffic (canary). Metric: tokens/sec per-GPU and p95 latency.
  * Implementation notes: maintain per-model rolling stats (last 5k requests), adjust batch_size in steps of +/-8, cap by max_batch for model.
  * Risk: oscillation -> add hysteresis (require 3 consecutive changes before commit).

- KV-cache compaction idea:
  * Problem: KV-cache growth for long-running chat sessions causes memory fragmentation and occasional OOM on lower-memory instances.
  * Idea: periodically compact/defragment on low-load windows; implement a GC pass that coalesces contiguous cache slabs and drops oldest prefix entries beyond policy.
  * Action: prototype compaction routine in runtime branch 'kv-compact-experiment'.

Kernel notes (fused-kernel fallback):
- Observed fallback path triggered when token_count % 16 != 0 for certain fused matmul kernels. Need to verify our alignment padding strategy.
- Action items:
  * Add validation harness that generates tensors with varied shapes to reproduce fallback deterministically.
  * Check whether pad-to-32 vs pad-to-16 changes perf and memory.
  * Confirm whether cuBLAS/cutlass version differences on A100s in our infra affect kernel availability.

Meeting / coordination:
- Sync with Luca and infra tomorrow 09:30 PT: go over kernel logs and plan for capturing additional perf counters.
- Quick sync with SDK team (Maya) to rollout retry backoff patch to beta users.

Personal TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add kernel-selection telemetry (deadline: 2026-04-09)
- [ ] Merge SDK retry jitter PR and monitor canary (PR 987)
- [ ] Kick off batching auto-tuner A/B test (set flags + dashboard)
- [ ] Prototype kv-compact GC loop (branch: kv-compact-experiment)
- [ ] Write short runbook for emergency rollback if compaction causes instability

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is there historical perf data correlating pad alignment changes to p99 on A100 v2 vs v3? (check infra benchmark buckets)
- If compaction GC is expensive, can we do incremental compaction instead of full-pass? Measure CPU cost first.

Random thoughts:
- If we can push small batching decisions into the router (micro-batches by latency class) we might reduce p99 for tail-heavy apps without sacrificing throughput. Worth prototyping.

End of scratchpad.
